mcqs.question: How does this broker's ordering guarantee actually work across a topic with multiple partitions?
options: Ordering is guaranteed globally across the entire topic, regardless of partition
There is no ordering guarantee anywhere in the system
Ordering is guaranteed only within a single partition, not across the whole topic
Ordering only applies to the first message ever published to a topic
mcqs.explanation: Ordering is a per-partition property: messages within one partition are strictly ordered by offset, but there's no defined ordering relationship between messages in different partitions of the same topic. This is a common misconception — assuming topic-wide ordering when only partition-level ordering is actually guaranteed.

mcqs.question: Why can a consumer that crashes and restarts simply resume from its last committed offset, with nothing 'specially recovered'?
options: The broker automatically retries every message for the consumer
Because messages aren't deleted on read — the log is unchanged, so re-reading from the stored offset reproduces exactly what the consumer would have seen originally
Offsets are stored on the consumer's local disk, so no data was ever at risk
Consumers in this design never actually commit offsets
mcqs.explanation: The retention model — messages persist after being read — is what makes this recovery trivial: the log at the stored offset is identical to what it was before the crash, so resuming is just picking up reading again. The broker doesn't auto-retry on the consumer's behalf, offset storage location isn't what matters here, and offset committing is very much part of this design.

mcqs.question: A broker acknowledges a producer's write as soon as the partition leader has it on disk, before any follower has replicated it. What durability risk does this create?
options: If the leader fails before followers catch up, the acknowledged message can be lost entirely, even though the producer was told the write succeeded
No risk — the leader's disk write alone is sufficient for durability
The risk only affects consumers, never producers
This only matters if the topic has a single partition
mcqs.explanation: Acking on leader-write-alone means the durability guarantee is only as strong as that one node — if it fails before replicating, an already-acknowledged message can vanish, breaking the producer's expectation. This isn't safe regardless of partition count, and it directly affects producers (who received a false success signal), not just consumers.
